subject: Selecting the correct amount of days and nights

messages.author: cc406a07d58437cd
messages.subject: Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
parts:
Hi Guys,

I am attempting to use the GGIR package for some of my data but am having trouble getting the outputs for the correct days and nights. I have tried a number of combinations of the different strategies, excludfirstlast and maxdur and days window. I can get the correct nights or correct days but not at the same time.

I am looking to get 6 days and 6 nights of data, in the study participants collected the accelerometers at various times throughout the day on a Monday, they then returned the accelerometer at the earliest on the next Monday. I have 50 participants and would like to look at the PA data for 6 days from waking on the Tuesday until sleeping on the Sunday, and 6 nights of sleep Tuesday through to Sunday. The only way I can see I can do it at the moment would be to use strategy 1 and alter hrs.del.start for each participant. Would you be able to give me some advise about how I may be able to run the entire sample at the same time? The A version of the code I am using is, I am using GGIR version 1.5-21:

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode= c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir= "C:/xxx/xxx",
             outputdir= "C:/xxx/xxx",
             studyname= "xxxx",
             f0= 1,
             f1= 3,
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,
             printsummary=TRUE,
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2,
             ndayswindow= 6,
             hrs.del.start = 0,
             hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 6,
             includedaycrit = 16,
             L5M5window = c(0,24),
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             timethreshold= c(5,10),
             anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(1),
             outliers.only = FALSE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 8,
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             excludefirstlast.part5 = TRUE,
             threshold.lig = c(50),
             threshold.mod = c(100),
             threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             boutcriter.in = 0.9,
             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
             boutdur.in = c(10,20,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
             timewindow = c("WW"),
             desiredtz = "Australia/Perth",
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             do.report=c(2,3,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,
             dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

This gives me the desired number of nights sleep 6 (Tuesday - Sunday) but 7 days of PA (Tuesday - Monday) and would like it to be 6 (Tuesday - Sunday).

Many Thanks. Robin

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
parts:
Hi Robin,
GGIR can only remove X numbers at the beginning and end, or exclude the first and last day.  If you want specific nights to be included or excluded and if these do not occur on the same day of measurement for each participant then best approach is to focus on the day and night specific output, and clean the data yourself by removing the nights or days you are not interested in.
Next, you can calculate the person average yourself.
Best wishes,
Vincent

parts:
Thanks for the reply Vincent. I am not sure if I was clear but I do want to look at the same time period for each participant.

I would like to exclude the first days wear, which would be part of a day as participants picked up accelerometers at different times throughout day one. I would then like to look at the following 6 days of PA data starting at waking on the second day, through until sleeping on the 7th day, and 6 nights of sleep data from going to sleep on the 2nd night through until waking on the 8th day.

If it is the same periods of measurement for each participant is there not a way to code it to just give these days as outputs and summaries and in file summary reports?

Many Thanks,

Robin

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
parts:
Hi Robin,

I see what you mean, but I am afraid GGIR as it is as the moment can only provide an approximation of this:
strategy = 2 will ignore the first day of measurement until midnight
and maxdays = 7 will ignore all measurement after 7 x 24 hours of data.

If you think this should be facilitate then:
- Create an issue on: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues
- Consider updating the code yourself and making a pull request
- If the latter is not possible, consider paying me for my time to do the work: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir

Best wishes, Vincent
